0.0.n: This is the family name of director Hayao Miyazaki, placed before his given name.

0.3.n: This is the family name of director and animator Yoshiyuki Momose.

0.5.n: Part of をはじめ, which introduces prominent examples at the start of a list.

0.6.n: Used with を to highlight leading examples, not to describe a chronological beginning.

1.0.n: This is the name of the Japanese animation studio.

1.1.n: Marks スタジオジブリ as the object of 支える.

1.2.n: The plain present form describes the directors and animators who sustain the studio.

1.3.n: Refers to film directors here; Japanese nouns do not need a plural ending.

1.5.n: A borrowed word for people who create animation, followed here by the group suffix たち.

1.6.n: This suffix marks a group of people, here the directors and animators.

1.7.n: Marks the directors and animators as the people doing the drawing.

1.8.n: The plain past form of 描く describes the works introduced in the next line.

2.0.n: Describes the collection as precious or hard to find, rather than merely expensive.

2.1.m: linking rare and valuable to collection
2.1.n: Connects 貴重 to the noun phrase 短編作品集 so it can describe the collection.

2.2.n: Refers to short films or animations here, contrasting with feature-length works.

2.3.n: Combines 作品, creative works, with 集, a collection.

3.0.n: 年 after a number identifies a calendar year.

3.1.n: Marks 1992 as the starting point of the time range.

3.2.n: 年 after a number identifies a calendar year.

3.3.n: Marks 2016 as the endpoint of the time range.

4.0.n: This proper name identifies the studio responsible for creating the films.

4.1.n: Marks スタジオジブリ as the subject of 手掛けた.

4.2.n: The plain past form of 手掛ける indicates taking responsibility for producing something.

4.3.n: A borrowed noun used before フィルム to specify the films' purpose.

4.4.n: Refers to filmed works here, not physical photographic film.

4.5.n: Links examples in an open-ended list, implying other types are included too.

5.0.n: Combines with クリップ to form the term for a music video.

5.1.n: In ミュージッククリップ, this refers to music videos rather than necessarily short excerpts.

5.3.n: A noun meaning company, used before CM to identify the type of advertisement.

5.4.n: This English-letter abbreviation is commonly used in Japanese for advertisements, especially television commercials.

5.6.n: Specifies that the animations are intended for online distribution.

5.7.n: A borrowed word referring here to animated works distributed online.

5.8.n: Placed after the examples to show that the list is not complete.

6.0.n: Forms the expression 数多く with 多く, emphasizing a large quantity.

6.1.n: The く-form of 多い combines with 数; 数多くの describes the large quantity of footage.

6.2.n: Connects 数多く to the following noun phrase, making it describe how much footage is included.

6.3.n: Emphasizes the special value or scarcity of the footage.

6.4.m: linking rare and valuable to footage
6.4.n: Connects 貴重 to 映像 so it can describe the footage.

6.5.n: Refers collectively to moving-image material, including the films and animations just listed.

6.6.n: Marks 映像 as the object of 収録.

6.7.n: A noun used as a shortened sentence ending; 収録しています would explicitly say the collection contains this material.

0.lit: Starting with Miyazaki Hayao and Momose Yoshiyuki,
0.tip: をはじめ highlights prominent examples, rather than saying who came first in time.

1.lit: Drawn by the directors and animators who support Studio Ghibli,
1.tip: Japanese puts descriptions before nouns: 支える describes the creators, and 描いた describes the collection in the next line.

2.lit: A rare and valuable short-work collection.
2.tip: This noun phrase completes the description begun in the previous line.

3.lit: From the year 1992 through the year 2016,
3.tip: から and まで mark the beginning and end of a time range.

4.lit: Promotional films that Studio Ghibli created, and
4.tip: や introduces an open-ended list that continues into the next line.

5.lit: Music videos, corporate commercials, web animations, and more,
5.tip: ほか after a list means additional unlisted items are included.

6.lit: Includes a large number of rare and valuable videos.
6.tip: Ending with 収録 instead of a full verb phrase creates a compact style common in promotional descriptions.
